record.paper_title: Open problems in some competition models
record.original_question: Consider the two-species Ricker competition system x_{n+1}=x_n e^{K-x_n-a y_n}, y_{n+1}=y_n e^{L-y_n-b x_n} on the positive quadrant, where K,L>0 are carrying capacities and a,b∈(0,1) are competition parameters. Its coexistence fixed point is ((aL-K)/(ab-1),(bK-L)/(ab-1)). Assume the local stability inequality 4(ab-1)+2(1-a)L+2(1-b)K ≤ (aL-K)(bK-L) < (1-a)L+(1-b)K holds. Is this coexistence fixed point globally asymptotically stable in the positive first quadrant for every parameter pair satisfying that inequality?

evidence.quote: In [2], the authors considered the Ricker competition model given by x_{n+1}=x_n e^{K-x_n-a y_n}, y_{n+1}=y_n e^{L-y_n-b x_n}, where (x,y) ∈ R_+^2. The parameters K, L > 0 are the carrying capacities of species x and y, respectively. Moreover, the competition parameters a and b are in the interval (0,1).
The coexistence fixed point (x^*, y^*) = ((aL-K)/(ab-1), (bK-L)/(ab-1)) of the Ricker equation (1) is asymptotically stable if 4(ab-1)+2(1-a)L+2(1-b)K ≤ (aL-K)(bK-L) < (1-a)L + (1-b)K.
Conjecture 1.2. Under condition (2), the coexistence fixed point (x^*, y^*) is globally asymptotically stable in the positive first quadrant, for all (K, L) ∈ Int(S_1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-species Ricker competition system on the positive quadrant $\mathbb{R}_+^2$:
$$x_{n+1} = x_n\, e^{K - x_n - a y_n}, \qquad y_{n+1} = y_n\, e^{L - y_n - b x_n},$$
where $K, L > 0$ are the carrying capacities and $a, b \in (0,1)$ are the competition parameters. Assume the coexistence fixed point
$$(x^*, y^*) = \left( \frac{aL - K}{ab - 1},\ \frac{bK - L}{ab - 1} \right)$$
lies in the open positive quadrant, and that the parameters satisfy the local stability inequality
$$4(ab - 1) + 2(1 - a)L + 2(1 - b)K \;\le\; (aL - K)(bK - L) \;<\; (1 - a)L + (1 - b)K.$$
Prove or disprove: for every quadruple $(K, L, a, b)$ satisfying these conditions, the coexistence fixed point $(x^*, y^*)$ is globally asymptotically stable in the open positive quadrant; that is, every orbit starting in $\mathbb{R}_+^2$ with $x_0, y_0 > 0$ converges to $(x^*, y^*)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that local asymptotic stability of the coexistence fixed point implies global asymptotic stability for the planar Ricker competition model remains open in full generality. Partial results exist: Ryals and Sacker, and later work by Bilgin, Gyllenberg, Jiang, Niu, and others, have established global asymptotic stability under additional technical assumptions, but the conjecture as stated has not been fully proved.

status_evidence.title: Global stability in the 2D Ricker equation (Ryals & Sacker)
status_evidence.snippet: Under a couple of technical assumptions, the interior equilibrium of the two-species Ricker model is globally asymptotically stable in the interior of the first quadrant, whenever it is locally asymptotically stable.
status_evidence.claim: Partial proofs of the global stability conjecture exist under extra technical assumptions.

status_evidence.title: A global picture for the planar Ricker map
status_evidence.snippet: Results increase support of this conjecture, but fall short of proving it.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is not fully resolved; further work has added partial support.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems and Conjectures in the Evolutionary Periodic Ricker Competition Model
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems and conjectures regarding global stability in Ricker competition models.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems in the literature.
